facts.statement: The study used a viral vector to boost the protein TFEB only in excitatory neurons of the hippocampus in young mice that carry a genetic model of Alzheimer's disease.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Boosting TFEB in these neurons lowered the amount of a toxic protein in the brain, reduced the number of protein clumps and damaged nerve endings, and improved the mice's ability to learn and remember locations.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The researchers found that the TFEB boost sped up the brain cells' waste-removal system and also improved the function of the cells' energy-producing structures.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: In a lab-grown cell line that produces the Alzheimer's protein, adding TFEB increased markers of the waste-removal system, boosted energy production, and lowered the amount of protein inside the cells.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: The authors conclude that activating this specific protein in brain cells early in the disease process helps clear toxic waste and protects against further brain damage.
facts.subject: animals
